Revert "CHROMIUM: Revert "mm: remove optimizations based on i_size in mapping writeback waits"" This reverts commit b96b564105d53e4318b34715577a6ba44aef901b. The above mentioned commit was a temporary fix which optimized calls to filemap_fdatawait_keep_errors() so that the range being waited upon was limited to the current size of the inode. This prevented excessive waits as described here: https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-block/msg38204.html and in the bugs in the BUG line below. However, we now have a real fix which is destined for upstream: https://patchwork.kernel.org/cover/11007125/ so use that instead. BUG=b:130521177, chromium:959968, b:133470926, b:65528573 TEST=Multiple iteration of dd from /dev/zero to /mnt/stateful_partition, filling the disk. Also, copied multi-GiB files from USB sticks to the Downloads folder via the GUI. I did this on bobba, sarien and samus-kernelnext. FROMLIST: jbd2: introduce jbd2_inode dirty range scoping Currently both journal_submit_inode_data_buffers() and journal_finish_inode_data_buffers() operate on the entire address space of each of the inodes associated with a given journal entry. The consequence of this is that if we have an inode where we are constantly appending dirty pages we can end up waiting for an indefinite amount of time in journal_finish_inode_data_buffers() while we wait for all the pages under writeback to be written out. The easiest way to cause this type of workload is do just dd from /dev/zero to a file until it fills the entire filesystem. This can cause journal_finish_inode_data_buffers() to wait for the duration of the entire dd operation. We can improve this situation by scoping each of the inode dirty ranges associated with a given transaction. We do this via the jbd2_inode structure so that the scoping is contained within jbd2 and so that it follows the lifetime and locking rules for that structure. This allows us to limit the writeback & wait in journal_submit_inode_data_buffers() and journal_finish_inode_data_buffers() respectively to the dirty range for a given struct jdb2_inode, keeping us from waiting forever if the inode in question is still being appended to. tast: Introduce chromeos-base/tast-build-deps. This CL introduces the chromeos-base/tast-build-deps package where build time dependencies of all Tast related binaries (test runners and test bundles) are put. This package resolves a few problems about interaction between Portage and Tast: - Portage has a bug that --onlydeps-with-rdeps=n is ignored in a certain situation (https://bugs.gentoo.org/682472) and Tast had to work around the bug in a hacky and incomplete way when installing build time dependencies. The hack is no longer required after introduction of this package since the new package has no runtime-only dependency. - Formerly users were prompted to emerge dependencies even just after running update_chroot because local test dependencies were not installed to the host, adding tens of seconds to the runtime of the tast command. Now those dependencies are installed by update_chroot, so there is no need of additional emerge. BUG=chromium:940761 TEST=./update_chroot TEST=./build_packages --board=betty Cq-Depend: chrome-internal:1387678 Cq-Depend: chrome-internal:1387312 Change-Id: I9d48c1a2c87a8da8c3774b8a8e124934d7122656 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1660509 Tested-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org>

BUG=b:132825853 TEST=network_WiFi_APSupportedRates Change-Id: Ica8c5a7a80ce7952745ab2f458b7ec98bdd046aa Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com> iwl7000-tree: a85747555140b0dc22ec88a1e0e6bac304a87dfe Signed-off-by: Luca Coelho <luciano.coelho@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1651854 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: iwl7000: mac80211: use STA info in rate_control_send_low() Even if we have a station, we currently call rate_control_send_low() with the NULL station unless further rate control (driver, minstrel) has been initialized. Change this so we can use more information about the station to use a better rate. For example, when we associate with an AP, we will now use the lowest rate it advertised as supported (that we can) rather than the lowest mandatory rate. This aligns our behaviour with most other 802.11 implementations. To make this possible, we need to also ensure that we have non-zero rates at all times, so in case we really have *nothing* pre-fill the supp_rates bitmap with the very lowest mandatory bitmap (11b and 11a on 2.4 and 5 GHz respectively). Additionally, hostapd appears to be giving us an empty supported rates bitmap (it can and should do better, since the STA must have supported for at least the basic rates in the BSS), so ignore any such bitmaps that would actually zero out the supp_rates, and in that case just keep the pre-filled mandatory rates. BUG=b:132825853 TEST=network_WiFi_APSupportedRates Change-Id: I102ba9fa6510971db586373afedaa5f8d39913c3 Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com> iwl7000-tree: 0ed4ba07be2d2d96efc925eb09d79446813780c9 Signed-off-by: Luca Coelho <luciano.coelho@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1651855 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

So do the low rate assignment anyway to help out drivers that might need it. power: Wait for external display on resuming with lid closed. Currently if the device resumes with lid still closed, we trigger lid closed action again. Also if the idle delay has expired, we trigger idle action too. This change as part of wake on Docked feature intends to wait for external displays for |KResuspendOnClosedLidTimeout|. This gives enough time for chrome to configure external displays if it recognizes one and tell powerd about it. Powerd on receiving a DisplayModeChange D-Bus call from chrome will treat it as user activity. Why wait here and not in SuspendDelayController ? SuspendDelays intend to give all deamons enough time to do stuff before suspend. Thus this should give chrome enough time to do the configuration. But chrome to prevent flicker in dark resume does not configure external displays when in suspend resume path. Thus let us not trigger suspendImminent immediately. Let us give chrome enough time to recognize external displays. BUG=chromium:786721 TEST=Deploy on nocturne and test the use case. Change-Id: I142493db5a73535d5016321c6545794fc10a97f4 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1651997 Tested-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@google.com>

pd_faft: Check the state transition messages with the correct port number There are 2 ports on the servo v4. When tests triggers some PD state transition, it tries to match the PD messages and parses the states. The matched pattern should have the port number; otherwise, it may match the unrelated port. For example, when DUT triggers PD hard reset, the servo v4 shows: > C1 HARD RST RX C1 st16 SRC_HARD_RESET_RECOVER C1 RECV fffe/7 [0]26019032 C0 Req [1] 5000mV 3000mA[1]5a417c3c [2]9a417d2c [3]00000000 [4]00000000 [5]00000000 [6]00000000 [249.117755 C0 REQ>1 C0 st6 SNK_REQUESTED CL: p0 s0 i500 v20000] C0 RECV 0943/0 C0 st7 SNK_TRANSITION C1 st14 SRC_DISCONNECTED C1 st15 SRC_DISCONNECTED_DEBOUNCE C0 RECV 0b46/0 C0 st8 SNK_READY [249.231203 CL: p0 s0 i3000 v5000] C1 st17 SRC_STARTUP C1 st18 SRC_DISCOVERY C1 srcCAP>1 C1 st19 SRC_NEGOCIATE C1 RECV 1042/1 [0]1004b12c Requested 5000 V 3000 mA (for 3000/3000 mA) C1 CTRL[3]>1 C1 st20 SRC_ACCEPTED C1 st21 SRC_POWERED C1 st22 SRC_TRANSITION C1 CTRL[6]>1 C1 st23 SRC_READY The original pattern matches the lines until "C0 st8 SNK_READY". However, this is C0, i.e. the CHG port, not the DUT port. This fix matches the lines until "C1 st23 SRC_READY". BUG=b:131840808 TEST=Ran firmware_PDResetHard on servo v4. When triggering some PD state transition, verified it matched the messages with the correct port number.
